Los Angeles County — Measure A (Charter Amendment Reiterating Good Faith Negotiation Obligations and Establishing Impartial Binding Arbitration for Certified Public Safety Employee Disputes)

positions.statement: "Measure A — Binding Arbitration for Labor Disputes [Oppose]" / "This measure would amend the LA County Charter to change how certain labor disputes are handled with a range of ‘public safety employees,’ among them sheriff’s deputies, firefighters, lifeguards, and medical examiners. For disputes involving ‘wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment,’ a binding arbitration process would settle negotiations between unions and LA County that have reached an impasse. Specifically, each side would select an arbiter, these two arbiters would select a third, and this three-person panel would be empowered to reach binding decisions, issue-by-issue, by choosing between the last offers put forward by each party. LA Forward recommends voting ‘no.’"

positions.statement: We have serious concerns about the most common progressive choice in this race, Rhonda Haymon. When we declined to endorse or recommend her 2024 run (against the judge who held her in contempt of court), the way she responded was one of the least professional reactions we’ve seen in our many years of doing endorsements. This behavior is mirrored in other public reporting. While we are reluctant to recommend prosecutors over public defenders, our concerns about Haymon leave us no choice but to suggest you vote for Maria Ghobadi who has extensive Democratic club and union backing, in addition to conservative support.

positions.statement: In this open race, there are two public defenders – Donna Tryfman and David Ross. According to Met News’ endorsement of Tryfman, she has a reputation for being more abrasive while Ross is more of a smooth talker. Both have extensive endorsements and would likely make good judges. subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: LA Forward strongly recommends a YES vote on Proposition 1, a $11.25 billion bond measure to fund affordable housing targeting the lowest income people across the state. Housing affordability continues to be one of, if not the biggest, challenge facing California. A third of renter households pay more than half their income on housing, while 80% of extremely low-income households pay more than half their income on housing. Put simply, that’s a million California households facing hard choices between groceries, needed healthcare, schoolbooks for their kids, and paying the rent.

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: Proposition 2 would double the cap on the state’s rainy-day fund (the Budget Stabilization Account, BSA) from 10% to 20% of annual tax revenue, and allow state lawmakers and the governor to use reserve funds to pay off state debt (but would not be required). Under current state law, California lawmakers may save only 10% of the general fund to the BSA. LA Forward suggests voters should support Proposition 2.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Proposition 41 would make any future attempt at passing special taxes more difficult by requiring an expensive, time-consuming audit prior to an election. VOTING NO allows voters the continued ability to directly determine the necessity and acceptability of any proposed special tax.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Proposition 42 would make any future attempt at passing special taxes more difficult by eliminating the ability to levy those taxes on certain kinds of wealth, like retirement savings and individually owned assets. VOTING NO gives voters the continued opportunity to directly vote on any proposed special wealth tax.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: Proposition 43 limits local voters' ability to fund essential local services and gives even more power to corporations. LA Forward strongly recommends a NO vote.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: At a time when community health providers are already facing significant financial uncertainty due to federal funding cuts, California should be strengthening its health care safety net and not creating another constraint that could reduce access to care. LA Forward recommends that you vote no on Proposition 44.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Proposition 45 makes major revisions to the California Environmental Quality Act (‘CEQA’), the 1970 state bill that mandates a process for including environmental protection in the approval process of developments throughout the state. For a broad variety of projects deemed ‘essential’ Prop 45 changes and limits both the CEQA review process by public agencies and the court review process for CEQA lawsuits. It also, again for ‘essential’ projects, establishes time limits for CEQA review, public comment, and CEQA litigation. LA Forward recommends voting ‘no’ on Prop 45.

LA Forward recommends Dr. Shirley Weber in re-election bid for California Secretary of State. In 2021 she was appointed by Governor Newsom to the position of Secretary of State to replace Alex Padilla. She won a statewide election in 2022 to continue in the role and is now up for re-election. She is formerly a professor of Africana studies at San Diego State University, a member of the San Diego Board of Education and served in the CA State Assembly from 2012 to 2020. During her time as Secretary of State Weber has prioritized expanding access to the ballot box for every voter and voter education and outreach.

LA Forward recommends incumbent Malia Cohen for a second four-year term. Cohen is backed by the California Labor Federation, California Environmental Voters, CA Council for Affordable Housing, California Nurses Association and more. Cohen has made addressing the housing crisis and expanding affordable housing priorities during her time in office. She used property tax abatements to stimulate affordable housing, backed AB 2353 which helps non-profit affordable housing developers secure the welfare property tax exemption and also approved $804 million in bond authority for affordable student housing. Cohen also led the way on property tax relief for those affected by the Palisades and Altadena fires. In addition to housing she has prioritized expanding health care, protecting the environment and equal rights as top issues of her campaign.
